chapter_title: The Seventh, concerning the Five Fathers
chapter_note: A well-preserved emanation hierarchy teaching: five fathers, each summoning three powers. The substrate is dominant in ¶2-12, forming a clean systematic sequence. Editorial fatigue is clearly visible from ¶13 onward, where the editors increasingly overlay institutional vocabulary (churches, elect, catechumens) onto the emanation scheme. The substrate identifications survive even in the second half, but the functional descriptions shift from cosmos→cosmos to cosmos→institution. The emanation pattern language ('after the pattern of') is structural substrate. A gospel citation (John 8:38) intrudes at ¶15. The chapter closes with a standard beatitude formula.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic frame: 'Once again the enlightener, our father [the] apostle of truth, is sitting in the midst of his disciples.' No cosmological content — purely hagiographic scene-setting.

paragraphs.core_text: Five fathers exist; they were summoned forth one of one. [Also], one did come out of another!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Thesis statement of the teaching. Establishes the emanation principle: five fathers, each coming forth from the previous. This is the structural kernel the entire chapter unpacks.

paragraphs.core_text: The first Father is the Father of Greatness, the blessed one of glory, the [on]e who has no measure to his greatness; who also is the first only-begotten, the first eternal; who exists with fiv[e fa]thers for ever; the one who exists before every thing that has existed, and that will exist.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First Father identified. Cosmological description: 'first eternal,' 'exists with five fathers for ever,' 'before every thing.' The doxological register ('blessed one of glory') is typical of substrate descriptions of the highest cosmic being. All attributes are cosmic.

paragraphs.core_text: Now he, the glorious Father, summoned from him three emanations. The [fi]rst is the Gre[at] Spirit, the first Mother, who came out of the Father. She appeared first. ⟨p.35⟩
paragraphs.temporal_note: First Father's three emanations begin. First emanation = Great Spirit / first Mother. Classic evocation/emanation language. 'Summoned from him' is the core verb of the emanation process.

paragraphs.core_text: The seco[nd i]s the Belo[ved of] the Lights, the great glorious Beloved, [the one w]ho is honour[ed; w]ho came out of the Father. [He ma]nifested ou[t of h]im.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second emanation from first Father. Note the heavy manuscript damage but the enumeration structure is preserved. 'Manifested out of him' parallels 'appeared first' — consistent emanation vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: The third father is the Thir[d Ambassador], the eldest of [a]]] the counsell[ors; who came out of] the first Father. He appeared.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third emanation from first Father. 'Eldest of all the counsellors' is a cosmic title. Manuscript damage but identification clear.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the first Father, the first power, the one from whom the three great powers came out. This is the first Father, the first eternal, the root of all the lights; from whom the three emanations came out. They have humiliated the Darkness. They have brought its heart's desire to naught. They have given themselves the victory. They have also given the victory to their aeons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary and cosmic-processual statement. Recapitulates the first Father, then describes the cosmic victory of the three emanations over Darkness. Both sides stay within the cosmic system: emanations vs. Darkness, victory given to aeons. 'Root of all the lights' is systematic cosmic vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: The second father, who came out of the first Father, is the Third Ambassador, the model of the King of lights. And again, he too summoned and sent out of him three powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second father identified as Third Ambassador. 'Model of the King of lights' is cosmic correspondence. Pattern language: 'again, he too summoned' establishes the recursive emanation structure.

paragraphs.core_text: One is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man; the one who bears up under all things; the great Pillar of blessing; the great porter, who is greater than all the porters.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First emanation of second father. Pillar of Glory as cosmic support structure — 'bears up under all things,' 'great porter.' These describe cosmic function, both sides within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is glorious Jesus the Splendour; [the] one through whom shall be given life eternal.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second emanation of second father. Jesus the Splendour is a cosmic figure (not the historical Jesus). 'Life eternal' describes his cosmic function — what this being provides within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the Virgin of Light, the glorious wisd[o]m; the one who takes away the heart of the [rul]ers and the powers by her image, as she fulfils the pleas[u]re of the greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third emanation of second father. Virgin of Light's cosmic function: seduction of the archons ('rulers and powers') through her image. Both sides cosmic — archons are cosmic beings, the image is a cosmic mechanism, the 'pleasure of the greatness' is cosmic will.

paragraphs.core_text: The third father, who came out of the second father: he is glorious Jesus the Splendour. And, again, he too summoned three evocations after the pattern of the second father.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third father identified. 'After the pattern of the second father' — the recursive pattern language is structural substrate. 'Evocations' used instead of 'emanations' or 'powers' — note vocabulary variation within the same teaching structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The first power whom he summoned is the Light Mind.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'the father of all the apostles, the eldest of [a]ll the [ch]urches; the one whom Jesus has appointed corresponding to our pattern in the holy church' — institutional layer. 'Father of all the apostles,' 'eldest of all the churches,' and 'our pattern in the holy church' map the cosmic being onto the Manichaean institutional structure. One side of the mapping exits the cosmic system.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First clear editorial seam in the chapter. The substrate identification ('the Light Mind') is clean, but the editor immediately bridges to institutional application. 'Our pattern in the holy church' is first-person institutional voice. Institutional score 13.89 confirms.

paragraphs.core_text: The second power whom Jesus summo[n]ed is the gre[at Jud]ge, who gives judgement on all the souls of mankind, [his] dwelling being established in the atmosphere under [ ... / ... ] wheel [ ... ] stars.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second emanation of third father. Great Judge's function (judgment of souls) and cosmic location (atmosphere, wheel, stars) are both cosmic — souls of mankind are the mixed light, the atmosphere is cosmic geography. Despite lacunae, the cosmic-locational description is preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: The third power is [the Y]outh, the gre[at ... ] light in his two persons, in [ ... ] that which has been established in the summons [and] the obedience.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'I am speaking about' (editorial first-person voice breaking the impersonal substrate register). Removed '[He] too [stood] with his fa[ther the] king [ ... ] the savio[ur ... ] seen, as he tells [ ... ] I, what I have seen with my Father, [I tell to] you. For yourselves, what you have seen [with your fath]er, do that.' — gospel citation (paraphrase of John 8:38). The citation enters via the NT, a 3rd-century editorial act.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavy manuscript damage obscures the original structure. The substrate identification (Youth, light in two persons, summons and obedience) is preserved. 'The summons and the obedience' (Call and Answer) is standard cosmic-processual vocabulary. The gospel citation is clearly late intrusion — 'I am speaking about' breaks from third-person to first-person, marking the editorial voice.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth father is the Light Mind. And, again, he too summoned three powers after the pattern of Jesus.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'the one who chooses all the churches' — institutional layer. 'All the churches' maps the Light Mind's cosmic function of selection/election onto the Manichaean institutional structure.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The emanation structure statement ('summoned three powers after the pattern of Jesus') preserves the substrate's recursive pattern language. The institutional clause is inserted between the identification and the emanation statement, a clear editorial interpolation.

paragraphs.core_text: The first power is the Apostle of Light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'the one who shall on occasion come and assume the church of the flesh, of humanity; and he becomes inner leader of righteousness' — institutional/editorial bridge. 'Church of the flesh' and 'inner leader of righteousness' describe the cosmic being's function in institutional terms, mapping cosmos→community.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Only the identification survives as substrate. The functional description, unlike earlier emanations (Pillar of Glory 'bears up under all things,' Virgin 'takes away the heart of rulers'), describes the being's role in human institutional terms rather than cosmic-processual terms. Editorial fatigue is evident — compare with the clean cosmic functions in ¶9-11.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is the counterpart, who shall come to the apostle and appear to him, becoming companion to him, sticking close to him everywhere; and providing help to him all the time, from all afflictions and dangers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The counterpart/twin (syzygos) is a standard cosmic being in the emanation system. Its function — accompanying and protecting the apostle — describes a cosmic relationship between two cosmic roles. 'The apostle' here is a cosmic role, not a historical person. Both sides stay within the cosmic system. Compare with Pillar of Glory 'bears up under all things' — same functional-descriptive register. Zero institutional vocabulary score confirms.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the Light Form.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'the one whom the elect and the catechumens shall receive, should they renounce the world' — institutional layer. 'Elect and catechumens' are Manichaean institutional categories. 'Renounce the world' is institutional practice. Institutional score 47.62 confirms this is the most heavily institutional paragraph in the chapter.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Only the cosmic identification survives. The functional description has been entirely replaced by institutional application. Compare with the Virgin of Light (¶11) whose function is described in cosmic terms — the Light Form's function is described entirely in institutional terms.

paragraphs.core_text: And also the fifth father is this Light Form; the one who shall appear to everyone who will go out from his body, corresponding to the pattern of the image to the apostle; and the thr[ee] great glorious angels who are come with her.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth father identified as the Light Form. Cosmic function: appearing at death ('go out from his body' = the soul's departure). 'Corresponding to the pattern of the image to the apostle' uses the substrate's recursive pattern language. The three angels are cosmic beings. Compare with ¶14 where the Great Judge 'gives judgement on all the souls of mankind' — same structure of cosmic being with function regarding human souls. Both sides remain within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: One (angel) ho[ld]s the prize in his hand. The second bears the light garment. The third is the one who possesses the diadem and the wreath and the crown of light. These are the three angels of light, the ones who shall come with this Light Form.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'and they appear with her to the elect and the catechumens' — institutional layer. 'Elect and catechumens' are Manichaean institutional categories, mapping the cosmic event onto the community.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The three-fold angelic description (prize, light garment, diadem/wreath/crown) is systematic correspondential enumeration — each angel carries a specific cosmic item. The summary 'these are the three angels of light' closes the substrate unit. The institutional application is appended as a final clause.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the five fathers who have come out of one another. They have appeared and man[ifes]ted through one another!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closing summary of the entire teaching. Returns to the thesis of ¶2 ('summoned forth one of one'). The seam flag ('These are the') is a false positive — this is a natural substrate summary, not an editorial bridge. No institutional vocabulary. Content is purely cosmological.

Classic devotional closure. 'Blessed is he who' beatitude formula, 'life eternal,' 'light garments given to the righteous' — standard exhortation vocabulary. Seam flag correctly identifies this as editorial extension of the teaching. Exhortation score 35.9 is the highest in the chapter.
